question.prompt: \(A\) takes \(m\) times as long to do a piece of work as \(B\) and \(C\) together; \(B\) takes \(n\) times as long as \(C\) and \(A\) together; and \(C\) takes \(x\) times as long as \(A\) and \(B\) together. Then \(x,\) in terms of \(m\) and \(n,\) is:

solutions.explanation:
For a fixed job, completion time is inversely proportional to work rate. Let \(a,b,c>0\) be the respective rates of \(A,B,C\), measured in jobs per unit time. Their combined rates add, so the given time comparisons become
\[
b+c=ma,\qquad a+c=nb,\qquad a+b=xc.
\]
Let \(T=a+b+c\). Using the total rate lets us express the first two rates without solving for their individual values:
\[
T=(m+1)a=(n+1)b,
\]
so
\[
a=\frac{T}{m+1},\qquad b=\frac{T}{n+1}.
\]
Subtracting these from the total gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
c&=T\left(1-\frac1{m+1}-\frac1{n+1}\right)\\
&=\frac{T(mn-1)}{(m+1)(n+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(m,n>0\), since they compare positive times. Because \(c>0\), this formula also shows that \(mn>1\); thus the denominator below cannot vanish. Finally, \(a+b=xc\) gives
\[
x=\frac{a+b}{c}
=\frac{m+n+2}{mn-1}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\dfrac{m+n+2}{mn-1}}\), choice \(\mathrm E\).
solutions.title: Express each rate as part of the total
